summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for her 21st cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She reported feeling well with no neurological or systemic symptoms. The chemotherapy was administered safely with urine alkalinization maintained throughout. She received fosaprepitant for nausea prophylaxis due to prior headaches with Zofran, and experienced mild nausea on day two, which resolved with ativan and compazine. Her methotrexate level at 36 hours was 0.13 micromolar, indicating safe clearance. A brain MRI showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence, with only stable chronic changes. She remained neurologically and hematologically stable. Aspirin was held during admission and restarted at discharge, with heparin bridging for DVT prophylaxis. She was discharged home in stable condition with a short course of oral leucovorin and instructions to continue her regular medications for chronic pain, asthma, and depression.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
